mina: Heads-up: onboarding run for `atlas-30b-int4` with 64k context on staging showed an odd token-order inversion around the 16k->16.5k handoff. not a soft drop — actual token duplication + reordering. filing here before i open an MR.

tom: whoa. duplication+reorder? any logs/snippet? :eyes:

yara: can you share the minimal repro or the exact flags you used?

mina: quick reproduction steps below. run `tests/longseq_harness.py` with `--model atlas-30b-int4 --context 65536 --prefill 18000 --seed 7`.

ops-bot: run triggered by mina: job=staging-longprefill-2091 user=min a flags=[model=atlas-30b-int4,context=65536,prefill=18000]

mina: log excerpt: 
```
[2025-03-02T09:05:01Z] prefill.start id=pf-2b7c total_prefill=18000
[2025-03-02T09:05:15Z] kvcache.page_alloc shard=1 pages=5 page_size=4096 window_start=12288 window_end=16384 page_hash=ab12f4
[2025-03-02T09:05:16Z] kvcache.page_append shard=1 page_idx=4 tokens=4096 page_hash=ab12f4
[2025-03-02T09:05:16Z] kvcache.handshake prefill_id=pf-2b7c page_hash=ab12f4 ok
[2025-03-02T09:05:17Z] decode.token 16380 tok=the prob=0.22
[2025-03-02T09:05:18Z] decode.token 16390 tok=is prob=0.19
[2025-03-02T09:05:19Z] decode.token 16405 tok=the prob=0.20  <-- duplicate + reorder
[2025-03-02T09:05:19Z] warning: kvcache.page_hash_mismatch expected=ab12f4 observed=ab12f4(merged)
```

mina: note the page_hash shows as merged in the warning which is weird; also observed `rope.offset_jump` warnings in the same window.

tom: interesting. different from a simple numeric drift — this looks like a race where two page writes / merges got interleaved and the decoder saw a reordered token stream. Could be kvcache merge on shard boundary + async prefill replay.

yara: did you test with larger page_size or different page alignment?

mina: yes: smaller page_size (2048) reduced frequency but didn't eliminate. bumping page_size (8192) made it rarer but when it hit it was worse (longer duplication stretches).

ops-bot: metric alert: prefill-error-rate for atlas-30b-int4 on staging spiked to 0.8% during run window.

ci-bot: deploy job 2091 finished. artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/2091/longprefill.log

tom: actionable hypotheses: 
- (A) async page-merge path has non-atomic page_hash reconciliation leading to transient merged markers that the consumer misinterprets as new page ordering;
- (B) RoPE offset recompute on page merge triggers a rewind and reapply that temporarily writes tokens out of order when replaying deferred writes;
- (C) quant int4 packing/unpacking edge-case on merge boundary causing buffer copy order inversion.

yara: we should reproduce with: fp16 (to rule out quant packing), int8, int4. also try disabling async_merge (flag `--kvcache-async-merge=false`) and disabling rope-recompute.

mina: i've queued a matrix: {runtype: staging-sweep-2100, variants: [fp16,int8,int4], flags: [--kvcache-async-merge=false, --rope-recompute=false, --kvcache-page-size=4096] runs=5}. ci-bot will show when done.

ci-bot: scheduled job 2100: matrix=[fp16,int8,int4] runs=5 flags=[--kvcache-async-merge=false,--rope-recompute=false,--kvcache-page-size=4096] ETA ~15m.

mina: initial local blind test: fp16 -> no duplication; int8 -> rare single-token repeat; int4 -> consistent multi-token repeat. so leaning quant-related but requires proving the merge race.

tom: mina, can you attach a side-by-side token diff for one failing trace (original vs rerun with async_merge off)? that will help isolate whether replay differs or underlying pages differ.

mina: will do. also adding `KV_PAGE_HASH_VERBOSE=1` env in the sweep so we capture per-page write hashes and ordering.

yara: if we confirm a merge ordering bug, short-term mitigation: force synchronous page commits at shard boundaries for onboarding quant models and add longprefill boundary checks to the onboarding checklist (especially at 8k,16k,32k).

tom: long-term: make page merge idempotent and include a monotonic sequence number in page headers so consumer ignores out-of-order merges.

mina: filing MR with failing trace + token-diff + proposed kvcache seqnum patch draft. will link when created.

ci-bot: job 2100 started. logs will appear at https://ci.internal/reports/2100/

mina: thanks team. tagging @yara for model-onboard checklist addition once we have final verdict. :thumbsup:
